$comment: What this build is allowed to make a noise with, and the evidence behind it.
Read before adding any audio file to the deployed tree. The rule this encodes:
nothing ships whose licence this repository can point at.
This file exists because the brief for the audio lane assumed the opposite of
what turned out to be true. It read: 'BGM and interface/card sound effects are
the safe, high-value core -- ship those', with only the ~147 general voice and
death lines flagged. That was checked before shipping, and it does not hold.
verdict: no audio file from the FreeKill checkout is shipped

sets.wasAssumed: safe -- engine chrome and the game's music, tracked upstream under GPL-3.0
evidence: Seven of the 28 files carry an intact third-party copyright notice in their ID3 tags. `egg1`, `egg2`, `flower1`, `flower2`, `fly1`, `fly2` each read `copyright=绯雨音乐`, `composer=绯雨音乐`, `TOPE=绯雨音乐`, `comment=www.LightRain.com.cn`; `gamestart.mp3` carries `TXXX=www.LightRain.com.cn`. Reproduce with `ffprobe -v error -show_entries format_tags -of default=nw=1 audio/system/egg1.mp3`.

绯雨音乐 (LightRain Music, lightrain.com.cn) is a commercial Chinese game-audio studio. Its own site lists four years of voice recording for 三国杀OL and the full audio production of 三国杀名将传. These are that studio's work-for-hire recordings with the copyright line still attached.
`bgm.mp3` carries `ENCODER=Lavc57.107.100 vorbis` with `genre=Blues` -- an Ogg Vorbis stream remuxed to MP3. A transcode chain, with no author named anywhere along it.
`chain.mp3` carries an Adobe Audition 23.3 (Windows) XMP edit history dated 2023-08-03 and no author.

The set was added to the repository in the same commits as the voice lines it was supposed to be distinguishable from -- `c6d883ec` 'Standard skills' carries sub-commits titled 'bgm', 'damage sound', 'card audio', 'skill audio' and 'death audio' together, and `851a3873` added `gamestart.mp3` and `ready.mp3` alongside fourteen `fastchat_*` voice lines.

The repository's GPL-3.0 grant is repository-scoped and its SPDX rollout (upstream issue #109) put `GPL-3.0-or-later` headers on .cpp/.h/.qml/.lua and on nothing else. A GPL grant is only effective from a licensor who holds the copyright; a contributor cannot license a recording they do not own by committing it.

sets.wasAssumed: safe -- equip sound effects, not performances
evidence: Not voice, but all three carry `encoder=Lavf59.27.100`, byte-identical to the fingerprint on `packages/standard/audio/death/caocao.mp3` and `packages/standard/audio/skill/fankui1.mp3` -- files the earlier audit had already ruled unsafe. Same conversion run, same source act.
No attribution of any kind anywhere in the tree.

These are not sound effects. `events/usecard.lua:43` builds the path as `.../audio/card/<male|female>/<card>` and dispatches on `player.gender` -- sound effects do not have a gender. They are ~0.5s recordings of a person saying the card's name, which is the same exposure as a skill line and the same one the earlier audit refused to clear.
`packages/standard_cards/audio/card/male/peach.mp3` carries `encoder=Lavf59.27.100`: identical to the death and skill lines.
The eleven non-gendered files at the top level (`blade`, `axe`, `crossbow`, ...) are equipment foley rather than speech, but share the same fingerprint and the same absence of attribution.

sets.wasAssumed: unsafe -- flagged by the earlier asset audit
evidence: Zero attribution; ID3 tags stripped to a bare `encoder=Lavf59.27.100`; scripts are the official 三国杀 lines verbatim.

The earlier audit could not establish whether these were re-performances or extractions and declined to guess. Nothing found since changes that, and the 绯雨音乐 notice on the sibling set makes extraction the more likely of the two.

sets.wasAssumed: unsafe, and too large to ship anyway
evidence: 887 of the 1773 files carry `album=绯雨音乐`; a further handful carry `artist`, `copyright` or `comment=www.LightRain.com.cn`, plus eleven double-encoded mojibake variants of the same string.
~887 files carry `encoded_by=Amadeus Pro`, a macOS audio editor -- an extraction toolchain, not a recording one.

The package names itself: `packages/mobile/pkg/mobile_rare/init.lua:8` reads `["mobile"] = "手杀"`, the official Yoka Games mobile 三国杀. Its git history includes commits describing copying official 原画配音 (original art and voice acting).
Not tracked by FreeKill itself; fetched separately by the in-app package manager.

whatShipsInstead.summary: Every sound the deployed site makes is synthesised in the browser at runtime by `src/room/audio/sfx.ts` and `src/room/audio/generative.ts`. No audio file is fetched, and `public/audio/` is empty in the public build.
whatShipsInstead.licence: Authored for this repository. Same licence as the rest of the source (GPL-3.0-or-later); no third-party recording is involved, and there is nothing to attribute.
whatShipsInstead.weight: 0 bytes of audio assets. The synthesiser is source, and it is in the room chunk.
whatShipsInstead.coverage: Every engine sound event is answered: card use, equipment, skill invocation, damage in all four elements, hp and max-hp loss, death, drawing, judgement, chain, recast, game start and game over. The engine's own categories choose the patch; within the card category the timbre is derived from the card's name, so a card that does not exist yet still gets a sound and no per-card table is ever written.

ifYouHaveALicence.how: `node src/room/assets/audio/build-audio.mjs --pack=<dir>` indexes a directory laid out the way the engine names sounds and emits `clips.generated.ts` plus `public/audio/`. Anything in the index is preferred over the synthesised patch at runtime; anything missing falls through to it. This is the same shape as FreeKill's own 资源包 mechanism, which the upstream project gitignores and treats as user-supplied.
ifYouHaveALicence.doNot: Do not point `--pack` at a FreeKill checkout and deploy the result. The evidence above is why.
